name: An oligo
description: one synthetic DNA oligonucleotide as ordered and as stored — its name, sequence, synthesis scale and purification, what it is for, and where its tube is
phrases: the shape of an oligo record

name.description: the lab's name for it, unique within the project. Project-specific nomenclature: SynThera's are oGho<n>, numbered without gaps, and the next available is one past the highest in that repository alone

sequence.description: 5'->3'. IUPAC ambiguity codes are meaningful: they are what makes a library a library. Case often marks intent — a designed mismatch, or the annealing region — and is not significant to any tool

scale.description: synthesis scale as the vendor names it

description.description: what it is for, in the words that will make sense a year later — 'Reverse p15A par A site library with 4 sites mutated', not 'reverse primer'

experiment.description: the experiment it was designed for

location.description: where the tube is, once it exists. Absent means not yet ordered or not yet filed

concentration.description: as labelled on the tube. 100 uM is the resuspended IDT stock; 10 uM is the PCR working stock; 2.66 uM is the sequencing working stock

notes: THE TAB-SEPARATED `<project>_oligos.txt` FILE IS THIS SCHEMA'S SERIALISATION AND IS ALSO THE IDT BULK ORDER FORM: name, sequence, scale, purification, one per line, in that order. That is why it has no header and why the column order is not negotiable — it is pasted into IDT's bulk input. The description and the location live elsewhere (the labsheet workbook, the inventory) precisely because IDT will not accept them. A record with a `location` is a tube; a record without one is an order.
